title: Parse a logfmt line
summary: Read key=value log lines with quoted values and escapes into a dict.
prompt: Your services log in **logfmt**, one event per line:
level=info msg="user logged in" user_id=42 dur=12ms
- Pairs are separated by one or more spaces; leading and trailing spaces are fine.
- `key=value`: an unquoted value runs to the next space. `key=` gives `""`.
- A value in double quotes may contain spaces and `=`; inside quotes, `\"` is a quote and `\\` a backslash.
- A bare `key` with no `=` is a flag: its value is `"true"`.
- If a key repeats, the last one wins. An empty line gives `{}`.
solution: while i < n and line[i] not in " =":
raise ValueError(f"unterminated quote in value of {key!r}")
template: Dojo.eq("plain and quoted values", {"level": "info", "msg": "user logged in", "user_id": "42", "dur": "12ms"},
parse_logfmt('level=info msg="user logged in" user_id=42 dur=12ms'))
Dojo.eq("= and spaces inside quotes", {"query": "a=b and c=d"}, parse_logfmt('query="a=b and c=d"'))
Dojo.eq("bare keys are flags, key= is empty", {"retry": "true", "debug": "", "level": "warn"},
Dojo.eq("extra spaces are fine", {"a": "1", "b": "2"}, parse_logfmt("  a=1    b=2  "))
Dojo.eq("an empty quoted value", {"msg": "", "x": "1"}, parse_logfmt('msg="" x=1'))
Dojo.eq("the last repeated key wins", {"a": "2"}, parse_logfmt("a=1 a=2"))
Dojo.throws("an unterminated quote raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: parse_logfmt('msg="oops level=info'))
wrong: for key, quoted, plain in re.findall(r'(\w+)=(?:"([^"]*)"|(\S*))', line):
hints: Splitting on spaces breaks quoted values; walk the line one character at a time instead.
Read a key up to a space or `=`. Then: space or end means a flag, `"` means a quoted value, anything else a plain value.
Inside quotes, a backslash means 'take the next character literally'; if you run off the end before the closing quote, raise.
